title: A trading day that pays for itself
target: How to run a single trading day so that it funds the next one, using only shop behaviour the game itself defines.
version: 1.6.0 (223), read from the copy of the game this site was built from (see the sources page)
prerequisites: A checkout you can stand at
Cash for at least one more order

steps.do: Set your prices before you open, not while a queue is waiting.
steps.because: the game prices goods in bulk through its own manager and keeps discounts in a separate system (BulkPricingManager, DiscountManager)

steps.do: Keep stock in storage so a shelf can be refilled during the day.
steps.because: storage sections and crates are modelled separately from the shelf (StorageSectionItem, Crate)

steps.do: Hold back a cash buffer to service any credit you took.
steps.because: a loan carries a tracked status and has its own repayment tab (LoanStatus, LoanPaymentsTab)

steps.do: Hire a cashier when the till becomes the bottleneck, not before.
steps.because: cashiers are a defined worker type with their own items (Cashier, CashierItem)

commonMistakes: Discounting everything instead of pricing deliberately.
Spending the buffer and missing a repayment.
Hiring staff before the shop has stock worth selling.
sources: A local copy of the game, read only. Grounding for each step is on the technical reference pages; no number is estimated.
